title: Subclinical hypothyroidism and the risk of coronary heart disease and mortality
authors: Rodondi N, den Elzen WP, Bauer DC, Cappola AR, Razvi S, Walsh JP, et al.
population: Individual participant data from 11 prospective cohorts in the Thyroid Studies Collaboration; 3450 with untreated subclinical hypothyroidism and 51,837 euthyroid
funder: Contributing cohorts were supported by public agencies and foundations; the thyroid testing in the HUNT Study was financially supported by Wallac Oy. The majority of the sponsors had no role in the design and conduct of the study; the National Institute on Aging and the Radiation Effects Research Foundation reviewed the manuscript and approved its publication.
result: 9664 deaths (2168 from coronary heart disease) and 4470 coronary events. Against euthyroidism, age- and sex-adjusted hazard ratios for coronary events were 1.00 (95% CI 0.86 to 1.18) for TSH 4.5 to 6.9 mIU/l (20.3 against 20.3 per 1000 person-years), 1.17 (0.96 to 1.43) for 7.0 to 9.9, and 1.89 (1.28 to 2.80) for 10 to 19.9 (38.4 per 1000 person-years); for coronary mortality 1.09 (0.91 to 1.30), 1.42 (1.03 to 1.95) and 1.58 (1.10 to 2.27).
